channelObservations: Titles start with familiar game experiences, contradictions or useful outcomes; specialist terms are supporting context.
Visible oddities include large doors, fake window interiors, mirrors, long hair, forgiving collisions and camera speed.
Concrete scene action, revealed paths/bounds and before/after states can supply evidence for the spoken claim.
Consistent two-line white/yellow headings and short lower captions aid recognition, but do not explain performance by themselves.

editorialAssessment.mainFinding: Choose an incident the viewer wants explained, then show the hidden rule that resolves it.
editorialAssessment.rejected300Gold: Familiar arithmetic and an unsurprising purchase goal gave little reason to wait for the answer; this does not mean reward-design topics cannot work.
editorialAssessment.currentFovDraft: Clear controlled visual comparison, but the opening is a parameter change before a strong gameplay question. A title and numerical difference alone may not create the desire to see the answer.
editorialAssessment.notTheMainDiagnosis: Do not attribute both drafts' editorial weaknesses to resolution, software, black margins or insufficient decorative motion.
editorialAssessment.thirtySecondImplication: The four selected references are approximately 67–75 seconds. For a 30-second Short, select one mechanism instead of compressing every subtopic.
selectionTests: Muted first two seconds show a surprising, understandable event.
The same incident can be replayed with one hidden condition exposed; the viewer can then predict a changed outcome.
The last five seconds resolve the opening incident specifically, rather than ending with a generic design moral.
